Regulation of collaborative learning (long event log)

Source: R/data.R
group_regulation_long.Rd

group_regulation_long is a coded dataset of the regulation actions of 2,000 students working in 200 small groups across three courses, one row per action with a timestamp. Each action is one of nine regulation moves: adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan and synthesis. Each student is classified as a high or low achiever (1,000 each), which makes the data suited to comparing the regulation pathways of two groups.

The data are in long format. Name the columns in context_tree() (actor = "Actor", time = "Time", action = "Action") or reshape them with prepare_input(); with the default 15-minute session gap, each student's actions form one sequence of 2 to 26 actions.

Usage

group_regulation_long

Format

A data.frame with 27,533 rows (actions) and 6 columns:

Actor

Integer student identifier, 1 to 2,000.

Achiever

Achievement level, "High" or "Low", constant within a student.

Group

Numeric collaboration group, 1 to 200; each student belongs to one group.

Course

Course, "A", "B" or "C".

Time

POSIXct timestamp of the action.

Action

The regulation move, the state of the sequence.

Source

Identical to group_regulation_long in the tna package (there a tibble), where it is described as generated synthetically from that package's group_regulation data.

See also

compare_groups(), prepare_input().

Examples

groups <- context_tree(group_regulation_long, actor = "Actor",
                       time = "Time", action = "Action",
                       group = "Achiever", max_depth = 2)
summary(groups)
#> <transitiontrees_group summary>  2 groups
#> 
#>  group n_seq n_obs n_nodes max_depth pruned logLik  df  nobs   AIC   BIC
#>   High  1000 13721      80         2  FALSE -22773 640 13721 46826 51643
#>    Low  1000 13812      82         2  FALSE -22968 656 13812 47248 52190
#>  perplexity
#>        5.26
#>        5.27
